intro_html: A loaded Tex-Mex skillet where beef, beans, corn, and rice all cook down together into one easy bowl. You get 52 grams of protein per serving for about $4.75 a plate (at everyday cost). It makes 14 servings, so batch it and forget it.
cost_closing_html: About $4.75 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls delivers 52 grams of protein and about 576 calories.
upsell_html: One skillet, a stack of containers, and your lunches practically make themselves. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Lean on dry rice by the bag at about a dollar-fifty a pound to bulk this out for almost nothing.
Canned beans, corn, and tomatoes are all cheaper in the store-brand cans, so build your cart there.
One bag of shredded cheddar stretches across the whole batch, so you do not need to grab two.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet and drain the grease.
Stir in the paprika and cumin and cook a minute to wake up the spices.
Add the diced tomatoes, black beans, and corn and let it all simmer together.
Fold in the cooked rice and stir until it is heated through and coated.
Top with shredded cheddar and let it melt before you dish it into bowls.
